html:
SMTO-EXE-0233 — The Docker registry refused this request

GUID: 62361dc7-5d1f-579b-83ed-be141cab16d6
Slug: docker-registry-denied
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: docker

What happened

  • The registry, the online store for Docker images, refused to let SMTO upload or download this image. The sign-in may be wrong or expired, or the account may not have access to that image.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Check the image name for typos, especially the account or team part, as in registry.example.com/team/app. Registries often refuse access, instead of saying 'not found', when a name points to an image you can't use.
  2. Open More options (the three dots), select Parameter Store, find the Docker registry parameter you used, and make sure the username and token are current. An expired or revoked token makes the registry turn the request away.
  3. On the registry's website, confirm your account may upload or download that image, or ask the image's owner to give you access. Even a correct sign-in is refused if the account isn't allowed to use that image.
  4. Then ask SMTO again, typing @ to pick the registry parameter. Sending the same request without a change will be refused again.

What success looks like

  • SMTO reports the upload or download finished and shows the image.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the registry account. Don't paste your token into the conversation, and don't keep repeating the same upload or download.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Gateway's Docker Engine returned 401/403 on an /images endpoint (pull, push or image read), which SMTO classifies as a registry denial.

What this means

  • The Engine returned an authentication/authorization denial on an image endpoint and classified it as registry_denied. It does not prove that refreshing credentials alone will grant the required operation. Docker execution remains on the selected Gateway and its explicitly configured local Engine. Preserve accepted private references, exact object identities, completed prefixes and unknown effects; diagnostics never replay a mutation.

Why this can happen

  • The Engine returned an authentication/authorization denial on an image endpoint and classified it as registry_denied. It does not prove that refreshing credentials alone will grant the required operation.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect image registry, repository and operation scope alongside accepted profile identity; distinguish authentication from missing repository permissions.

How to fix it

  • Verify the repository path in the image reference and that the docker_registry Parameter's username and token are valid and have pull or push rights on that repository (test with docker login and docker pull or push from the Gateway host). Fix the credential or repository permission before resubmitting; do not loop unchanged push or pull requests.
  • Correct the established registry identity, credential or repository permission prerequisite; do not repeatedly push or pull unchanged requests.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect the exact object identity, typed arguments and selected Gateway capability; correct the reported prerequisite before a new request.

How to verify the fix

  • The exact authorized repository operation is permitted using the intended private profile.

What not to do

  • Never automatically replay an uncertain Docker mutation.

Technical notes

  • Docker execution remains on the selected Gateway and its explicitly configured local Engine. Preserve accepted private references, exact object identities, completed prefixes and unknown effects; diagnostics never replay a mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
